title: Declarative response-contract layer + graceful stream rejections
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Introduce a declarative response-contract validator and streaming rejection event. Backward compatible by default; opt-in strict mode available via per-route config or request param. See migration notes in docs/response-contracts.md.
description: Motivation: Many downstream integrations require a contract on model outputs (structured JSON, typed objects). Previously we had ad-hoc checks scattered across the streaming and non-streaming paths which caused inconsistent failure modes and surprising partial streams. This PR introduces a single declarative 'response contract' layer that can be bound to routes/models and validates model outputs against a JSON Schema-like contract. Key goals: 1) Make validations deterministic and pluggable; 2) Provide a consistent, machine-readable failure signal in streaming responses so clients can detect and react to schema failures; 3) Keep default behavior backward-compatible (permissive mode) while offering strict enforcement for customers that opt in.

review_comments: Ethan Morales (2026-02-19): Nice approach. Two concerns: (1) streaming behavior needs a clear client contract; can we emit a final event type instead of throwing connection reset? (2) Where do we log the failed payload for debugging without exposing PII?

Author Priya Shah (2026-02-19): Addressed by adding a 'schema_reject' terminal event with an attachable small error bundle ID (not full payload). We added a server-side retention TTL and KMS-protected blobs for internal debug retrieval behind enterprise audit controls.

Lina Chen (2026-02-21): Tests failing in CI for the TS SDK mapping; schema enum coercion differed between python and ts. Also please add a migration note for routes using existing 'response_format' strings.

Author Priya Shah (2026-02-22): Fixed TS coercion; added explicit normalization layer and migration doc section. Added a compat shim that accepts legacy response_format values and maps them to contracts.
Marco Ruiz (2026-02-23): For strict mode turned on, will we reject partial streams mid-sequence? We need deterministic behavior for tool/function-calling workloads.

Author Priya Shah (2026-02-23): We introduced three strictness levels: permissive (default: annotate but allow), strict (reject entire response and return schema_reject), and fallback (attempt repair via a configured postprocessor then accept or reject). For streaming, strict immediately emits schema_reject and closes the stream to avoid downstream partial-state. For fallback mode, we attempt a single postprocess correction and emit either an accepted final object or schema_reject with correction hint.
Ethan Morales (2026-02-24): Approved after tests and docs updates. Verified metrics hooks for schema failures are present.
Lina Chen (2026-02-25): Small nits in docs phrasing and an added example for tooling callers. Approved.

merge_summary: Squashed 9 commits into main. Added response-contract registry, streaming schema_reject event, SDK mappings, tests, and docs. Opt-in strictness modes exposed via route config and request param 'strict_mode'.
migration_notes: Default behavior is permissive: existing routes unchanged. Operators who want strong validation can enable per-route 'response_contract' with strict_mode: strict|fallback. For OpenAI-compat paths, legacy 'response_format' values are automatically mapped to contracts but operator can override. Rolling upgrade: deploy server changes, then enable contracts on a small percentage of traffic using rollout APIs before broadening.
observability_changes: New metrics: response_contract.validation_count, response_contract.failure_count, response_contract.repair_attempts. Stream events include schema_reject with error_code 'SCHEMA_MISMATCH' and debug_blob_id when available.
backwards_compatibility: By default unchanged. SDKs expose new helpers but continue to accept old params. We ship compat shims in the server for legacy values. Customers must opt-in to strict enforcement.
